title: Session 06 — Approach to Ironhold
html:
Session 06 — Approach to Ironhold

The Wayward Company completes the caravan run into Ironhold, arrives at last light through the northern gate, meets Ironhold — and, after a long day, hears Vrass’s first whisper. The Heart of Ironhold ask lands. Session 7 opens with the party deciding whether to try.

Session opener (read aloud at the table)

Where you are and what you’re doing. You signed on with Brenna Hartwell at Kolt’s Depot for a caravan escort south to Ironhold — three of you, one wagon of your own, hauling Sylas’s two undead labourers and a fresh draft horse called Valor. The Wayward Company. It was meant to be a straight run — get the caravan to Ironhold, get paid, use the town as a base for whatever came next. It has not been a straight run. On Day 2 you stopped at Stillbrook and picked up Sera Vey, a wounded refugee whose sister Mira and Mira’s two children were taken by a man called Halvor over a debt — she needs to reach Ironhold to find them, and Torren’s read on her (natural 20) said she is telling the truth. Then Vrass landed on the road. You talked your way out of a fight nobody was going to win: Torren swore lifetime servitude to the dragon in exchange for your lives; Vrass took the contract wagon and half the manifest; and while the negotiation was happening, Sylas quietly moved the sealed Coin Cipher chest from the wagon into his Bag of Holding. Vrass flew off thinking he had everything. He didn’t. Nobody outside this camp knows the chest is still with you — not Brenna, not Sera, not the merchants waiting in Ironhold.

Ironhold’s smelting glow has been staining the northern sky since noon. Now it’s the last of the light and you’re camped a stone’s throw from the northern gate, close enough to hear the guards’ bell mark the hour. Brenna is bedded down by her wagon — small camp, quiet camp, just her and you. Sera Vey has kept the fire between herself and the Wayward Company wagon since dusk; the two zombies unnerve her and she is not going to pretend otherwise, so she’s rolled up in a borrowed blanket on the far side of the coals, sleeping in fits. Valor stamps once and settles. Inside Sylas’s Bag of Holding, the sealed iron-bound chest with the eclipse seal sits exactly where he put it two days ago when a young black dragon named Vrass landed on the southern road and took everything else. Vrass got the contract wagon, half the manifest, and — for the price of the party’s lives — Torren. A lifetime oath, sworn in earnest, with a dragon’s parting words: “We will speak soon.”

The gate opens at dawn. What would you like to do?.

Table decisions locked in for Session 6

  • Beat 1 (Vrass’s lair detour): SKIPPED. Party chose to press on to Ironhold at end of Session 5. Do not offer the detour in-fiction.
  • Beat 7 (Veris encounter): STAGE FLEXIBLE. Prep all three venues (Kettle late evening, Merchants’ Quarter next morning, Envoy’s Rest if sought). Run whichever fits the party’s movements. Default: Kettle late evening.
  • Beat 8 (Vrass’s first whisper): READ ALOUD AT THE TABLE. DM’s call — table won’t metagame, and hearing it lands the moment for everyone. Deliver the whisper text in full, at the table, in Vrass’s voice, whenever Torren is in a still moment (the whisper reaches him — but the players hear it too).

Open state

  • Location: camped just outside Ironhold’s northern gates. Day 4 morning of the caravan run.
  • Party level: 6.
  • Party name: The Wayward Company.
  • With them: Brenna Hartwell (caravan master), Sera Vey (hidden in the Wayward Company wagon), two zombies (Sylas’s), Valor (draft horse).
  • Carrying: the sealed Coin Cipher chest hidden in Sylas’s Bag of Holding. Everything else is visible.
  • Live bond: Torren is sworn to Vrass. Dark bond active. First whisper is coming.

Session goals (DM)

  1. Land the party in Ironhold. Make the town feel real — smoke, forge-glow, sergeant at the gate, the Grey Kettle.
  2. Seed the Kellan framing plot via ambient chatter and refugees.
  3. Introduce Envoy Veris in the town (not on the road). Sylas’s purple-tiefling colouring registers with Veris — this is Sylas’s Aurora Peaks bloodline moment.
  4. Deliver Vrass’s first whisper on the Heart of Ironhold. Give Torren a real deadline (three weeks to the dark moon).
  5. Set up the Coin Cipher slow-burn — Wesley Halloran’s runner Petran collects at the yard and hears from Brenna directly; Wesley’s inquiry begins that same night.
  6. Sera enters Ironhold with the party. She waits with them through the yard and asks them for help by evening — the Halvor hook lands for Session 7.

Beat structure

Beat 1 — Vrass’s lair detour — SKIPPED for Session 6

Party chose at end of Session 5 to press on to Ironhold. This beat is unrun and archived here in case they double back later.

(Original content: half-day off the southern road, rocky overhang, foul stream, wreckage of Wagon 2 stripped, Vrass’s lair empty because he is out hunting, hoard present per Vrass. Chest is not there — Sylas has it. ~30 min table time if run.)

Beat 2 — The road in (morning of Day 4)

The last morning of the road. Camp packed at first light, gate a couple of hours ahead. As you climb the last ridge and drop toward the northern approach, two things layer over each other — the countryside going quietly wrong, and the trickle of people going the wrong way.

The countryside. Subtle Naturus corruption signs seep into what the party sees over the first hour of the ride:

  • Two farm fields side by side — one flourishing, one blackened at the roots, no obvious cause.
  • A brackish ditch that shouldn’t be brackish, running past a well that a farmer refuses to draw from.
  • A dead sheep in a hedgerow, no visible wound; the flies won’t touch it.
  • A dog barking at nothing across a low stone wall, refusing to stop, until its owner drags it inside.

Nature check DC 14: this is not Vrass’s acid. This is something else — the shape of the Frostwood Marsh corruption they heard about at Stillbrook. If a player connects it: Kaelith’s rot is finding new vectors along the southern road. She is unknowingly riding the Cairn-Bound leak — the party does not know that yet.

The refugees. In the second hour, closer to the gate, they pass two small carts moving north away from Ironhold. Tired families, tarps over their possessions, quiet children.

  • A greying human woman on the front cart, arm bandaged, reins loose in her hands.
  • A stocky dwarf man on the second cart, brown beard streaked with iron dust, staring at the road.
  • Three children between the two carts, one of them still crying occasionally.

If the party greets them, the woman speaks first:

“A smith refused the gold and lost his son’s apprenticeship overnight. That’s my sister’s boy. Sixteen years old. Twelve years to make master. Gone in a morning.”

If pressed, the dwarf will name Corvan Drake, spit sideways off the cart, and add “the Aurum coin came in a purse we didn’t want.” They do not know the political detail — they know the outcome.

Second thread if a party member asks the right question (“has anyone else been leaving? / any other news?”): the dwarf mentions a “Coldhearth notice” on the Aeloria board — a fenling village dying, asking for help. Not a Session 6 pull — a seed for later. See Coldhearth for the hook.

Atmospheric only. Do not stage combat. Let the mood do the work.

Beat 3 — The Northern Gate (midday)

The road drops out of the foothills and the town rises to meet you. Ironhold at midday is bright, loud, and full of smoke — the southern sky over the town is a permanent haze from Foundry Row, but overhead the sun cuts through and the sandstone walls glow warm.

The gate itself. The Northern Gate is smaller than the ceremonial southern gate but not lightly held — Ironhold-cut sandstone, an oak-and-iron door, a portcullis raised for the day, two flanking towers with archer slits. A short queue: two farm wagons ahead of the caravan, a family on foot behind. Watchmen in green-and-brown livery lounge in the shade of the wall. A papers table sits under an awning to the right — a scarred oak trestle with a leather-bound ledger and a stub of pencil.

Sergeant Gorren works the table today. Human, mid-fifties, weather-tanned, thick moustache, patched greens. Bored, honest, thorough. He knows Brenna by sight and by name.

  • He processes the caravan on Brenna’s word. She names each remaining crate; he writes what she tells him. He asks after the missing wagon. Brenna says the truth: “A young black dragon took it two days south of Stillbrook.” Gorren blinks twice, writes it down verbatim, and does not comment.
  • Sera walks in with the party — no fuss. Ironhold does not turn people away at the gate. She’s on foot, tired, no papers, but neither is half the north-road traffic today. Gorren asks her name and reason. She tells him: “Sera Vey. Looking for my sister.” He writes it down and waves her through with a small nod. No suspicion, no interrogation.
  • The party. Standard question — “business in Ironhold?” — followed by whatever the party answers. Nothing they say will get them turned away today.

Before they leave the table, Gorren offers directions. He glances at Brenna, then at the party, and points down the main street:

“You’ll be wanting a bed. Grey Kettle in the Merchants’ Quarter — clean, discreet, good wine, Mother Hessa runs it. Broken Anvil in Rustpocket if you want cheap and loud. Ashfall in Stonecut’s dwarf-run and won’t take you without an introduction, so leave that one alone until someone vouches for you. Kettle’s your best bet. Tell Hessa I sent you.”

He also mentions the caravan yard is straight through the gate, first left, in the shadow of the inner wall.

Beat 4 — The Caravan Yard (early afternoon)

Description. A wide packed-dirt yard just inside the northern wall, walled on three sides by warehouses and stables. Iron rings sunk into the ground for tethering horses, a long water trough down the eastern wall, a shaded loading ramp along the south side. Sacks and crates stacked in orderly rows against the warehouse doors. The yard smells of horse, dung, dust, and hot iron drifting down from the foundries. Perhaps thirty people working — porters unloading, merchants inspecting crates, a couple of Watch guards keeping an eye on the ledgers.

Ambient patrons — pick two or three for texture:

  • Two dwarves in leather aprons hauling ingots off a Celestium-Clan wagon, arguing loudly and cheerfully about the weight in a language you don’t recognise.
  • A thin human clerk with an ink-stained sleeve, moving between crates with a slate, ticking each off with the concentration of a man who does not want to make a mistake today.
  • A tiefling teamster in a dust-caked red coat, sitting on a barrel eating an apple and watching everyone without appearing to.
  • A small group of Watch guards near the yard’s exit gate, sharing a flask, bored.
  • Two porters — half-orc man and human woman — running crates from a wagon to the warehouse, moving in a wordless rhythm.

Brenna works the yard. As merchants and agents arrive to collect their consignments, she tells each of them what happened on the road — Vrass, the wagon lost, the sealed chest gone with it. She is honest, brief, and clearly tired. Reactions range from resigned nods (this happens on frontier caravans) to a small merchant who swears once and walks off. Nobody blames the party. Brenna pays the party’s promised twenty-five gold here, hand to hand, no ceremony.

The party’s own Wayward Company wagon is set aside near the south wall. They can leave it here (yard fees are low — 2 cp per night) or move it to whichever inn takes them (the Grey Kettle has yard space; the Anvil does not).

Petran arrives. Late in the yard hour — perhaps thirty minutes after Brenna’s first announcement — a man in a plain grey merchant’s coat walks in from the south gate. Ordinary height, ordinary build, sandy hair, soft-soled boots. He does not look at the party. He goes straight to Brenna.

  • He speaks briefly with her. Two short questions: “Was the chest specifically taken, or was it in a wagon that was taken?” and “Did anyone see it open, damaged, or moved?” Brenna answers plainly. He nods. He does not linger. He walks south into the Merchants’ Quarter.
  • He is Petran — Wesley Halloran’s runner, mid-tier Coin Cipher. Wesley begins his quiet inquiry that evening. He is not a Session 6 threat.
  • Party noticing Petran: passive Perception 14 to clock a man specifically waiting for a specific missing crate rather than general delivery. If Torren watches him leave, Perception + Insight spots that Petran’s body language reads Cipher runner, not merchant. Insight DC 15 to place him as network. Torren’s Guilded Veil / former Watch background gives him advantage here.
  • If the party follows Petran — see the Petran file for the full trail; he walks a professional route and ends at the Halloran Cloth Emporium in the Merchants’ Quarter.

Slow-burn: the party can build interest in this thread now (approach Petran, notice him, follow him) or let it play out as ambient consequence. Their choice.

Beat 5 — Sera’s ask

Sometime during or just after the yard — while the party is deciding on an inn, or while the wagon is being moved, or over a cup of something at the yard’s tea-stall — Sera thanks Brenna and thanks the party. She hangs back for a moment and asks whether anyone will help her find her sister.

  • She does not push. She has learned by now not to expect help.
  • She names Halvor. She does not know exactly where his compound is; she has a name and a general direction (Council Ward). If the party agrees, they’ll go in the morning.
  • She has no coin. She offers what she has: honest labour, whatever the party needs, whenever they need it.
  • If the party accepts, this hooks Session 7’s Halvor confrontation.

She’ll take a bed wherever the party takes one — she isn’t asking for her own room, she’ll sleep on a common bench if that’s what the inn offers.

Beat 6 — Choosing an inn, and settling in (afternoon into evening)

Three options in Ironhold. All three are described here so the party can choose without the DM leaving the sheet.

Option A — The Grey Kettle (Merchants’ Quarter) — Gorren’s recommendation, default

The house. Three-storey timber-and-stone on the main east-west street of the Merchants’ Quarter, two blocks from the Council Ward’s outer gate. Above the door hangs a large grey enamelled kettle from a wrought-iron bracket — thirty years in the same spot. The taproom is long, warm, and well-lit: bar down the left, tables and benches for sixty, broad fireplace on the back wall. A curtained snug on the right seats six comfortably. Kitchen behind sends out fresh bread at seven, noon and six. The place smells of yeast, rosemary, and hot pewter.

Prices. Single room 5 sp, double 8 sp, master 2 gp. Breakfast included. Supper 1 sp standard, 5 sp premium (mutton pie and cheese board). House wine 2 sp / carafe; Merchants’ Quarter red 8 sp. Party rate: master room at the double rate if Brenna vouches or if Hessa warms to them (she will).

Innkeeper. Mother Hessa. Warm without being sentimental. Twenty-eight years running the place. Will not sell information; may hint if the party earns her by the end of the evening.

Patrons in the room this evening — pick two: - Two moneychangers at a corner table, sleeves rolled, working an abacus and a small pile of foreign coin. Human and half-elf, both middle-aged, laughing quietly at something the abacus just told them. - A guild secretary at the bar, thin man in a black coat, reading correspondence over a mulled wine and making the occasional small note in a leather journal. - A Drake-adjacent merchant — heavy-set, gold rings, laughing too loud at his own jokes — dining with two junior colleagues who are laughing on cue. - Bryndis Ashveil’s protégée Ana Kest eating quickly at a small table by the kitchen — foundry apron folded on the bench beside her. - Mara Volk at the third table from the front window, alone, small book in hand, tea gone cold — she watches the room in the reflection.

Envoy Veris is not here tonight. He took supper here the past two evenings and the staff have started expecting him. If the party asks, Hessa will say only “he may come. He may not. He was here yesterday.”

Kettle rumours (pick two to overhear during the evening): - “The Blades Guild vote is close. Ashveil is old but she is not finished.” - “Drake bought two suppers for Councillor Halven last week. The bribable ones do not need much.” - “The Aurum envoy has been here a week. Nobody knows what his exact terms are yet.” - “Kellan Bracewell was seen — no, she was not seen, ignore that.” - “Halvor of the Council Ward has been looking terrible.” - “Refugees on the north road. Something about a smith and his son.”

Option B — The Broken Anvil (Rustpocket) — cheap, loud, real

The house. Two storeys of soot-stained timber at a Rustpocket street corner, sagging slightly to the east. Sign above the door: a broken anvil, half the paint worn away. Taproom the length of the building — long bar down the left, mismatched tables and benches for eighty at a squeeze, rough hearth burning at the back. Kitchen is a serving-hatch. Rear door opens into an alley network. Smells of ale, sweat, and hot lard.

Prices. Common dormitory bed 1 sp, private single 3 sp. Breakfast 2 cp (bread, hard cheese, thin stew). Supper 4 cp standard, 1 sp premium (a pie that is either the best or the worst in Ironhold depending on the day). House ale 1 cp; drinkable ale 3 cp; the good ale 6 cp.

Innkeeper. Riven. Watches everything. Says almost nothing about what he watches. Ends fights in three rounds.

Patrons — pick two: - Foundry crew off shift — six men and two women, soot still on their forearms, drinking hard, laughing hard, arguing about a shift bonus that didn’t come through. - A lone Watch corporal at the front table, front to the door, drinking too fast — this is Corporal Vasso (Tuesday and Friday nights only; skip if it isn’t one of those). Talks to strangers who buy him ale. - A quiet halfling in a corner with his back to the wall, one ale, one small knife on the table in front of him — this is Bram off his Drake’s Furnace shift. - A group of Rustpocket labourers — half-orc, human, two dwarves — arm-wrestling for coppers and losing badly to the dwarves. - Denny Bracewell — a young broad-shouldered human man in an apprentice’s rough tunic, drinking alone, watching the door. He does not know his sister Kellan is Guilded Veil.

Anvil rumours: - “The Blades and the Ingots almost went at each other outside the Furnace last week.” - “Vasso has been shouting at his beer again. Something about promotion.” - “Refugees on the north road. Ironhold-adjacent kids getting turned out of apprenticeships.” - “They say the Aurum envoy paid a Watch corporal for a private conversation.” - “Someone saw a black carriage go north at dawn.”

Option C — The Ashfall (Stonecut Ward) — will not take them tonight

The house. Half-set into the western cliff face, three of its back rooms literally carved into the rock. Dwarven-cut stone worked to look almost timber, a stone slab sign with three descending flakes. Low-ceilinged taproom, dwarven-scale benches, a permanent hearth that has not gone out in ninety-one years. Smells of dwarven-bread yeast, malt, and the mineral tang of the cliff behind.

Innkeeper. Grust. Ninety-one years running the house. Polite. Quiet. Notices everything.

But — outsiders cannot walk in and be served. Grust will politely turn the party away tonight and redirect them to the Kettle. Introductions that would open the door: a word from Torvi (Stonecut elder), from Bryndis Ashveil, from Ana Kest, or from Sergeant Gorren (grudgingly). If the party thinks to name Gorren at the door, Grust considers it, grunts, and takes them. Otherwise: Kettle. This is a Session 7+ location for them if they earn it.

(Prices for completeness if the party earns entry later: dormitory 4 sp for humans, private single 5 sp, cliff-cut back room 1 gp. House ale 2 cp, dwarven dark 5 cp, Grust’s private stock 1 sp when available.)

DM default: unless the party pushes hard elsewhere, they end up at the Kettle. Brenna drops in during the evening and mentions the party’s arrival to Hessa. Sera takes a common bed on the Kettle’s first floor for 2 sp (Hessa waves the fee if the party mentions Sera’s story).

Beat 7 — Envoy Veris crosses their path (flexible venue)

Prep all three venues. Run whichever fits the party’s movements.

  • Kettle late evening (default). Veris arrives around ninth-hour, in the snug, with two men Hessa does not recognise. Warmer register — the wine has been going for an hour. He notices the party across the room, finishes his conversation politely, and drifts over.
  • Merchants’ Quarter next morning. Cooler, more businesslike — the party’s crossing his street on the way somewhere else, and he stops them with a polite word.
  • Envoy’s Rest in the Council Ward (if the party seeks him). Envoy’s Rest is Ironhold’s Council-Ward guesthouse for foreign delegates — a two-storey stone building with a small walled garden, staffed by two Council servants and a Watch officer at the door. Veris receives visitors in a sitting room off the entrance hall. Most controlled register — he is at home here.

In every venue: Veris is polite, condescending, and coolly curious. He offers the party a moment of his time.

  • He notices Sylas’s colouring immediately. Light purple skin — that colour of tiefling is a rare anomaly, and Veris (Kaelthorn cousin, wizard, interested in bloodlines) knows what it means. “Aurora Peaks blood — and not just any blood. The old curse-line. Fascinating. May I ask your house?”
  • Sylas can decline to answer. Veris does not press. He notes it either way.
  • Consequence: Veris files Sylas mentally. If the party sees him again in Session 7, he engages Sylas warmly and with pointed interest. See Veris for the wizard/collector context and Selene for the downstream reporting arc — Selene’s Crystal Shards hear of Sylas within a fortnight.

Common folk looking at Sylas see “unusually pale purple, but he’s a tiefling — they come in odd colours.” Only educated observers (Veris, Vaeloran, a Sylvarian scholar, a Silver Crescent monk) recognise the curse-line marker.

Beat 8 — Vrass’s first whisper (late, after the tavern quiets)

Wherever Torren is when he is alone — his room, a quiet corner of the Kettle, walking back from the privy — the whisper lands.

“Little sworn-halfling. Listen carefully.... I have an assignment for you.”

“There is a stone in this town. A jewel that glitters like fire. They call it the Heart of Ironhold. Steal it and bring it to me before the dark moon. Do not fail me in this small thing.”

The dark moon is roughly three in-game weeks away. Vrass has given Torren a real deadline. See The Heart of Ironhold for full item mechanics and consequences.

Delivery: read aloud at the table (DM’s decision — the table won’t metagame and hearing it lands the moment for everyone). Deliver Vrass’s voice in full, at the table, whenever Torren is in a still moment — his room, quiet corner, walking back from the privy. Frame it clearly as “only Torren hears this” even though the players do. The rest of the party learns as much or as little as Torren chooses to tell them in-character.

Session ends here. Long enough beat for the table to absorb the ask.

NPC roster for Session 6

  • Brenna Hartwell — caravan master, contract settled at the yard, parts ways.
  • Sera Vey — hidden in the Wayward Company wagon, thanks the party, asks for help.
  • Envoy Veris Caelthorn — in Ironhold for a week. Encounters the party at the Kettle, in the Quarter, or at Envoy’s Rest. Recognises Sylas’s Aurora Peaks curse-line.
  • Sergeant Gorren — Northern Gate papers table. First Ironhold face.
  • Petran — Wesley’s runner. Beat 4. On-screen briefly at the caravan yard, then walks south to report.
  • Wesley Halloran — off-screen. Learns of the lost chest from Petran that evening. Begins his inquiry overnight.
  • Mother Hessa — Grey Kettle. Warm welcome.
  • Councillor Halven — off-screen, named in Beat 6 Kettle rumours. Political texture for Session 7.
  • Vrass — whisper only. The Heart ask.

Location pointers

  • Ironhold — town overview.
  • The Grey Kettle — likely lodging.
  • Warehouse 14 — off-screen consequence.
  • The Heart of Ironhold — the ask.
  • The Coin Cipher Chest — hidden in Sylas’s Bag of Holding.

Live threads exiting Session 6

On the table: - Vrass’s Heart of Ironhold ask (Torren) — three-week deadline. - Sera’s help request (Halvor confrontation next session). - Aurum envoy’s contract vote pressure — Bryndis vs Drake. - Coin Cipher inquiry — Wesley starts asking questions overnight. - Refugee gossip — Kellan framing hinted. - Sylas recognised by Veris (delayed consequence — a Selene report reaches Aurentium in maybe two-three sessions).

Simmering off-screen: - Kaelith’s operations continue in the Aelorian Territories. - Vaeloran’s Stage 3 ritual — ongoing at slower pace (per revised lich progress structure). - Verdant Expanse Corruption Countdown — 2 sessions. - Vroth-Khorn Seal Clock — 4/6 (unchanged; Vrass has not yet moved on the Bog Hag).

Party doesn’t know yet: - Sylas hid the chest → Aurek expected it, Veris was the recipient. - Wesley Halloran exists. - Veris has begun quietly thinking of Sylas as an Aurora Peaks bloodline asset. - Kellan Bracewell is Guilded Veil and framed by Drake. - The Six Wardens and the Vroth-Khorn cosmology.

Pacing notes

  • Three hours of table time. Beat 2 (the road in) runs tight — 20–30 minutes total, countryside signs and refugees back-to-back. Beat 3 (the gate) — 15–20 minutes. Beat 4 (the yard) — 30–45 minutes; this is where the Petran seed lands and where Brenna wraps. Beat 5 (Sera’s ask) — 5–10 minutes. Beat 6 (the inn) — 45–60 minutes; let them settle. Beat 7 (Veris) — 10–15 minutes, weighty. Beat 8 (Vrass’s whisper) — 5–10 minutes to breathe.
  • Do not stage combat this session. The road threats are atmospheric. Ironhold does not fight the party on arrival. Save combat for Session 7 if needed.
  • The Veris encounter (Beat 7) is a soft threat. Play him warm and cold at once. Sylas’s player should feel the encounter, not be lectured about it.
  • Read Vrass’s whisper aloud at the table (locked at top of doc). Frame clearly as “only Torren hears this.” The players hear it because they need to know why Torren is quiet for the next scene; they will not metagame it.
